text: {"observations": "From 0 to about 2.7 s, harmonic lines descend steadily, which looks like a motor spinning down. A short silence follows, then at about 4.6 s an abrupt broadband onset with harmonics rising quickly to a steady level, a motor spinning up. The tone holds steady (top harmonic near 6.2 kHz) from about 5 to 7.3 s, then spins down again with broadband noise underneath. This pattern of motor spin-up and spin-down with airflow noise and stable whine harmonics fits a vacuum cleaner being switched on and off. It does not fit frying (crackling broadband with no harmonics), a washing machine (slow drum rhythm, sloshing) or typing (discrete clicks).", "answer": "C"}
